parameters.name: ain
parameters.description: Effective inlet conversion coefficient: `ain*flow` adds pressure from metered air. Estimated jointly with the other independent coefficients at both fitting stages described below.

parameters.name: weight
parameters.description: Fraction of open-valve conductance assigned to `1-(valve/vfull)**3`; the complement multiplies `1-3*(valve/vfull)**2+2*(valve/vfull)**3`. Both basis functions decrease with closure and vanish at the seat. Estimated jointly at both stages.

parameters.name: cap
parameters.description: Maximum small-overpressure relaxation-rate scale at the open valve. Estimated jointly with the other independent coefficients, with `0.03 <= cap <= 0.5` 1/s to make the near-atmospheric dynamics resolvable by one five-second RK4 step.

parameters.name: eps
parameters.description: Pressure scale for smoothing the ideal square-root cusp near atmosphere. Estimated jointly at both stages, with `0.01 <= eps <= 0.5` bar; this is an effective laminar/low-Reynolds-number crossover correction, not independently measured hardware.

parameters.name: gopen
parameters.description: Open-valve conductance, tied to the fitted slope and crossover scale so the restoring slope is bounded without an additional penalty in the pressure-fitting criterion.

parameters.name: patm
parameters.description: Atmospheric reference pressure, `patm = 1` bar, supplied approximately by TASK.md and here assumed exactly; not adjusted to reduce simulation errors.

parameters.name: vfull
parameters.description: Fully closed valve normalization, `vfull = 100` %, from TASK.md. Clamping `Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)` restricts the conductance extension to the physical stroke.

parameters.name: back
parameters.description: Subatmospheric restoring rate, `back = 0.1` 1/s, chosen as a ten-second numerical vacuum-relaxation time, not estimated. `-back*Min(p-patm,0)` is a valve-independent extension outside normal pressurized operation, not an identified leak or a model of real reverse valve flow.

estimation.criterion: Final criterion: sum of squared free-run errors on pressure `p` in bar after each trajectory’s first sample, with no state correction. This matches long-horizon evaluation and avoids treating the filtered derivative `dp` as an independent instantaneous measurement. One-step pressure-transition squared error is only an initialization criterion.
estimation.data: Final coefficients use all 1452 rows of data/train.csv and all 1454 rows of data/val.csv as two separate trajectories, without joining their endpoints. There are 1451 and 1453 fitted pressure transitions. Initial samples set each free-run initial condition and are not residuals. The derivative column `dp` is not used for final estimation. The independent training-only comparison and first-two-thirds blocked comparison in fixed_atmosphere.py were used to assess structure generalization; only after these checks were both entire trajectories used to improve coefficient coverage. No rows were removed for outlier or transient handling and no test data were accessed.
estimation.method: Bound-constrained nonlinear least squares using the Trust Region Reflective algorithm in scipy.optimize.least_squares (SciPy 1.18.1). Reference: SciPy official least_squares documentation, checked in this round. Nonlinearity and physical bounds make a direct linear solution inapplicable. All four independent parameters were estimated together in each of two stages. First minimize squared one-step RK4 pressure-transition errors, starting at `ain = 0.0013` bar/(s*(l/min)), `cap = 0.35` 1/s, `eps = 0.1` bar, `weight = 0.5`; these broad positive guesses are close to preliminary mass-balance fit scales and avoid a vanishing-conductance start. That stage yielded `ain = 0.00130996705873` bar/(s*(l/min)), `cap = 0.5` 1/s, `eps = 0.0464955052904` bar, `weight = 0.592780024848`. Then, starting at those values, minimize squared full free-run pressure errors and obtain `ain = 0.00129146940365` bar/(s*(l/min)), `cap = 0.40624523958` 1/s, `eps = 0.0847309256747` bar, `weight = 0.499732246491`. The numerical bounds were `0.0001 <= ain <= 0.005` bar/(s*(l/min)), `0.03 <= cap <= 0.5` 1/s, `0.01 <= eps <= 0.5` bar and `0 <= weight <= 1`. The gain is broadly positive, the crossover stays nonsingular, the weights enforce a monotone valve map, and the rate ceiling avoids an unresolved atmospheric-pressure cusp during a five-second RK4 step. Both stages use two-point finite-difference Jacobians, `x_scale = "jac"`, linear loss, and relative stopping settings `ftol = 1e-11`, `xtol = 1e-11`, `gtol = 1e-11`; maximum function evaluations were 1000 and 1500 respectively, with actual solver counts 18 and 26. Each simulation is one classical RK4 step per `Ts = 5` s with the current logged inputs held constant. Numba 0.68.0 compiles the loops; no random sampling or seeds apply. Fixed and tied parameters are not optimization variables. The function guards excursions beyond 20 bar with a finite penalty; neither final fitted training trajectory approaches that guard.

discussion.family: Lumped isothermal ideal-gas inventory balance with a regularized Bernoulli/orifice discharge law. Bernoulli discharge supplies the square-root pressure-drop asymptote; the analytic cusp smoothing and monotone cubic valve map are empirical additions, not claimed to follow exactly from Bernoulli’s equation.
discussion.interpretation: Define `z = Max(p-patm,0)` bar and `g = (gopen*(weight*(1-(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)+(1-weight)*(1-3*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**2+2*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)))` in sqrt(bar)/s. The term `ain*flow` is the effective ideal-gas inlet contribution. The outlet contribution `(gopen*(weight*(1-(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)+(1-weight)*(1-3*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**2+2*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)))*Max(p-patm,0)/(Max(p-patm,0)**2+eps**2)**0.25` is nonnegative, asymptotes to `g*sqrt(z)` at overpressures large compared with `eps`, and is approximately `g*z/sqrt(eps)` near atmosphere. This smoothly represents a low-pressure linear regime rather than an ideal orifice cusp. The tie `gopen = cap*sqrt(eps)` makes the largest outlet restoring slope equal to `cap` at an open valve and atmosphere. `weight` controls the monotone valve stroke curve; it is not a physical valve area. The term `-back*Min(p-patm,0)` is a valve-independent numerical vacuum extension outside the fitted pressure regime, not a leak.
discussion.origin: The inlet term and square-root pressure dependence came from a fixed-volume isothermal mass balance and Bernoulli/orifice reasoning. Linear discharge gave substantially biased high-pressure simulations, and unconstrained pressure-power fits favored an exponent close to one half. The ideal square root is non-Lipschitz at atmosphere; exploratory near-zero smoothing scales produced excessive slopes for a five-second numerical step. Therefore the delivered family uses positive fitted smoothing with an explicit fitted restoring-slope bound. This regularization is a modeling choice, not a discovered physical law. The valve map was an empirical monotone cubic choice; a third positive basis coefficient was essentially zero and removed after exploratory fitting. Exponential and power-opening maps were also tried but did not give a compelling validation improvement. No genetic symbolic-regression search supplied this expression.
discussion.limitations: The effective inlet volume, valve area, discharge coefficient, temperature, bubble holdup and calibration cannot be separated from these two pressure/input trajectories. No flow-delay, thermal or actuator state is present. On an independently simulated validation trajectory, the earlier training-only fit gave RMSE 0.039234 bar; first-two-thirds fits gave fresh-initialized tail RMSE 0.025531 bar on training and 0.055572 bar on validation. Final all-data refitting gave training RMSE 0.026510 bar and validation RMSE 0.037919 bar; these last two are fitting diagnostics, not independent validation. Final one-step residual correlations with the next-minus-current inlet-flow change are -0.766 on training and -0.658 on validation, showing missing timing/dynamics that the autonomous single-state form cannot resolve. Alternative future-flow diagnostic fits reduced transition errors but were excluded because future inputs are not arguments. The fully open and sealed endpoints are extrapolated: training stroke spans approximately 10.31 to 92.41 %, validation 1.63 to 94.45 %. The subatmospheric term has no identified physical validity. Absolute pressures far outside the observed approximately 0.99 to 2.19 bar range, thermal transients, liquid-level changes and negative inlet flows are not validated. The fitted crossover scale is not small compared with typical overpressures, so the regularization materially affects the result and must not be represented as a harmless numerical epsilon. R1: `ain > 0`, so increasing `flow` always increases `dp`. R2: for `0 <= weight <= 1`, both cubic stroke basis functions are nonincreasing in closure, the pressure-drop discharge is nonnegative, and the subatmospheric term does not depend on closure; hence increasing `valve` cannot decrease `dp`, including in the implemented vacuum extension. R3: at `flow = 0` and `p = patm`, all terms vanish, with `patm = 1` bar. R4: for any not-fully-closed valve and `flow = 0`, `dp < 0` above `patm` and `dp > 0` below it, so atmospheric equilibrium is attractive. R5: at `valve = vfull`, the conductance is exactly zero, so for `flow >= 0` the derivative `ain*flow-back*Min(p-patm,0)` is nonnegative. No unexplained outlet leak remains at the sealed seat. These are structural properties, not conclusions inferred just from observed samples.
